biography: Marco Billi, a product of Sao Paulo's vibrant karting scene, didn't come from motorsport royalty. His father, a mechanic, instilled in him a love for engines and a relentless work ethic. Marco honed his skills on the unforgiving Interlagos karting track, often scavenging for discarded tires and meticulously rebuilding his kart after each session. His big break came at 19, winning the Brazilian National Karting Championship. A subsequent move to formula cars showed promise, but inconsistent funding plagued his early career. He finally secured a Porsche Junior driver spot at 24, showcasing raw pace but also a frustrating tendency for costly errors. Now, at 28, Billi is in his prime, a Porsche stalwart. He is known for flashes of brilliance punctuated by moments of questionable decision-making, making him a compelling but unpredictable figure on the grid.
drivingStyle: Billi's driving style is a high-risk, high-reward affair. He's known for his aggressive late-braking maneuvers and willingness to push the car to its absolute limit. Tire management is not his forte; he often burns through his rubber early in a stint, sacrificing consistency for outright speed. He thrives under pressure, often pulling off spectacular overtakes in the closing laps, but is equally prone to making critical errors when the stakes are highest. Billi’s approach is simple: attack first, ask questions later.
rivalries: Enzo Rossi: A longstanding rivalry stemming from their karting days, intensified by several on-track collisions and accusations of unsportsmanlike conduct.
Isabelle Dubois: A battle for supremacy within the Porsche team, fueled by constant comparisons and a clash of personalities.
Kenji Tanaka: A rivalry born from a controversial overtake in the final corner of the 24 Hours of Le Mans, resulting in Tanaka crashing out of the race.
quirks: Always wears the same pair of lucky socks, even if they are full of holes.
Listens to a specific Brazilian samba song before every race.
Refuses to eat anything green on race day.
famousQuote: "Second place is just the first loser. You either win, or you learn...usually the hard way."
careerHighlight: Winning the 6 Hours of Interlagos in 2022 after starting from the back of the grid, overcoming a penalty and a late-race puncture to snatch victory on the final lap.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the final hour of the 24 Hours of Daytona in 2021, costing his team a likely victory and earning him significant criticism.
